report_name: North Korea's TraderTraitor Group Linked to Record $6.3B Binance Heist

threat_actors.name: TraderTraitor
threat_actors.description: A North Korean state-sponsored threat actor, associated with the Lazarus Group, attributed with high confidence to the theft of approximately $6.36 billion from the Binance cryptocurrency exchange on October 29, 2026. The group exploited a multi-signature protocol to execute massive, unauthorized withdrawals.
threat_actors.goals: Financial gain to fund the North Korean regime.

threat_actors.name: Lazarus Group
threat_actors.description: Notorious North Korean state-sponsored threat actor that TraderTraitor is associated with.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Likely used for initial access by targeting a Binance engineer, leading to a compromised developer environment.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The attackers likely gained access to and used legitimate credentials to operate within Binance's environment after the initial compromise.

attack_patterns.name: Financial Theft
attack_patterns.description: The primary objective and final action of the attack campaign, resulting in the theft of approximately $6.36 billion in digital assets from Binance's hot wallets.

attack_patterns.name: Service Exhaustion Flood
attack_patterns.description: Rapid, high-volume transactions were executed to overwhelm manual review processes, effectively causing a denial of service for human intervention during the heist.

attack_patterns.name: Web Protocols
attack_patterns.description: Used for command and control and to interact with the Binance exchange's systems to execute unauthorized withdrawals.

identities.name: Binance
identities.description: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, which was the victim of a $6.36 billion heist attributed to the TraderTraitor group.

identities.name: TRM Labs
identities.description: A blockchain intelligence firm that attributed the Binance heist to the North Korean group TraderTraitor.

identities.name: Chainalysis
identities.description: A blockchain intelligence firm that attributed the Binance heist to the North Korean group TraderTraitor.

identities.name: Elliptic
identities.description: A blockchain intelligence firm that attributed the Binance heist to the North Korean group TraderTraitor.

identities.name: Tether
identities.description: The issuer of the USDT stablecoin, which collaborated with Binance to freeze a significant portion of the stolen funds.

identities.name: Circle
identities.description: The issuer of the USDC stablecoin, which collaborated with Binance to freeze a significant portion of the stolen funds.

infrastructure.name: Compromised Developer Environment
infrastructure.description: A compromised developer environment at Binance served as the entry point for the multi-stage attack, allowing the threat actors to manipulate transaction approval systems.

indicators.name: Anomalous EIP-7702 Multi-Signature Approval
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous EIP-7702 Multi-Signature Approval
id: 2b9a1f8c-7d3e-4b0a-9c1d-8e7f6a5b4c3d
status: experimental
description: Detects log entries indicating anomalous or potentially unauthorized approvals related to the EIP-7702 multi-signature protocol, which was abused in the Binance heist.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-31
references:
  - https://www.forbes.com/sites/digital-assets/2026/10/30/binances-63-billion-hack-started-with-one-engineers-laptop/
tags:
  - attack.t1078
level: high
logsource:
  category: application
detection:
  selection_protocol:
    Message|contains: 'EIP-7702'
  selection_keywords:
    Message|contains:
      - 'unauthorized'
      - 'suspicious approval'
      - 'failed validation'
      - 'bypassed'
  condition: selection_protocol and selection_keywords
indicators.description: Detects log entries indicating anomalous or potentially unauthorized approvals related to the EIP-7702 multi-signature protocol, a method reportedly abused in the Binance heist.

indicators.name: Rapid Swapping of Stablecoins to ETH
indicators.pattern:
title: Rapid Swapping of Stablecoins to ETH
id: 8c4d5e6f-1a2b-4c3d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects log entries indicating a rapid swap from stablecoins (USDT, USDC) to decentralized assets like Ethereum (ETH), a common laundering technique used by North Korean actors after a heist.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-31
references:
  - https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/binance-exploit-latest-findings-and-response/
tags:
  - attack.t1657
level: medium
logsource:
  category: application
detection:
  selection:
    Message|contains|all:
      - 'SWAP'
      - 'TO:ETH'
    Message|contains:
      - 'FROM:USDT'
      - 'FROM:USDC'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects a pattern of rapid swapping from stablecoins (USDT, USDC) to decentralized assets like Ethereum (ETH), a common laundering technique to evade asset freezes.
